items.title: MACC postpones recording of Isa Samad's statement over health
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has postponed recording the statement of former Felda chairman Datuk Seri Isa Samad until his health improves. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Isa was currently receiving treatment at Serdang Hospital after undergoing eye surgery. "We will resume recording his statement after receiving an update on his health status from the Prisons Department.

items.title: Two Myanmar nationals held after allegedly assaulting policeman
items.summary: RAUB: Two Myanmar nationals were arrested after allegedly assaulting a policeman who had reprimanded them for playing loud music by the roadside at Kampung Pamah Kulat in Dong here early today. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a corporal, was alerted by villagers before going to the scene to conduct checks. Azry said both suspects were detained shortly after the incident.

items.title: MG S5 packs strong value into an electric SUV
items.summary: THE MG S5 EV has become one of the more interesting electric SUVs in Malaysia, particularly after its transition from fully imported (CBU) to locally assembled (CKD) production thie year. At first glance, the S5 EV does not look radically different from the growing number of electric SUVs on Malaysian roads. The locally assembled S5 EV LUX Long Range produces 203PS and 350Nm, compared with 170PS and 250Nm in the earlier CBU model.

items.title: When will Melaka vote? EC to decide key state election dates on October 7
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on October 7 to discuss matters related to the 16th Melaka state election. EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the special meeting followed the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly last Wednesday. “The special meeting will be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.

items.title: MMA calls for stronger healthcare workforce measures in Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has urged the government to prioritise healthcare workforce retention, stronger screening and follow-up care, and greater private-sector involvement in Budget 2027. Its newly appointed president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan said Malaysia could not afford to wait until workforce shortages became more severe, citing data showing that 3,494 doctors left the Health Ministry between 2019 and 2023. Sivanaesan said Budget 2027 should also address policies that made it harder for doctors and specialists to build sustainable careers in public healthcare.

items.title: Easy money: Man loses RM301,777 to scam by mystery sender in whatsapp
items.summary: TEMERLOH: A plantation worker lost RM301,777 after falling victim to a bogus investment scheme sent to him through an anonymous WhatsApp message, police said. The 51-year-old oil palm worker from Kuala Krau not only used his savings, but also borrowed money from his siblings and friends to participate in the scheme. Temerloh police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the victim claimed that he received the message from an unknown number on Aug 11.

items.title: Three days of fun, entertainment at Jom Heboh Segulai Sejalai Sarawak
items.summary: MIRI: Karnival Jom Heboh Segulai Sejalai Sarawak 2026 returns to Sarawak after a 19-year absence, with the three-day event starting at Miri Boulevard today. The booths will give visitors opportunities to enjoy entertainment, obtain information, take part in interactive activities and access services offered throughout the carnival. The Health Ministry is also offering dental services to visitors, alongside other health-related activities.

items.title: Haze forces Kuching Marathon 2026 cancellation at eleventh hour
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Kuching Marathon 2026 scheduled for Sunday (September 27) has been cancelled due to the prevailing haze situation affecting Kuching and surrounding areas. In announcing the cancellation, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) said it had been continuously monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and other environmental indicators since the onset of the haze. He also said more than 13,000 participants had registered for this year’s Kuching Marathon.

items.title: Two expected to face charges over Kedah fertiliser distribution
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigation into the matter had been completed and the case classified under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009. "The MACC prosecution division will refer the case to the Attorney-General for further action. "If the Attorney-General gives consent based on our recommendation, the charges may be registered in court next week or the following week," he said at a press conference today.

items.title: Two ex-Felda officers to be charged over KLVC project
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Two former senior Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) officials being investigated over alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project will be charged next week. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the Attorney-General had given consent yesterday to prosecute the two. "Meanwhile, the other person, the former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Commission, will face two charges under Section 417, and the charges will be brought on Sept 29," he said at a press conference today.

items.title: Saravanan, family ordered to declare assets to MACC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan, his wife and their three children have been ordered to declare their assets to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said notices under Section 36 of the MACC Act would be served on Saravanan, his wife and two of their children at the MACC headquarters on Monday, while another child studying in London would receive the notice in November. "Saravanan, his wife and two of their children would be present at the MACC headquarters to receive the notices, while another child who is studying in London would receive the notice in November.

items.title: Witness confirms seeing confidential email to Petros top officials, but unsure of sender
items.summary: Petronas human resources division manager Suhaidah Labu, 42, said she saw the email, which was allegedly sent by former manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni to Petros chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Janin Girie and chief financial officer (CFO) Azha Jalil Abdul Jalil. Suhaidah said this while testifying in the trial of Khairul Akmal, who is accused of attempting to disclose confidential Petronas documents to Petros in June 2024. Suhaidah: Correct.

items.title: Vietnam stocks fall 2.2pct in first week after FTSE market upgrade
items.summary: HANOI: Vietnam's benchmark fell 2.2 per cent in the first week after the country's formal inclusion in FTSE Russell's secondary emerging market index, according to LSEG data. The index's decline wiped about US$7.4 billion off its market value up until Sept 24 this week, HoSE data showed. Since the start of the year, foreign investors havecut their exposure to Vietnamese stocks by nearly US$37 billion.

items.title: Malaysia strengthens bonds with Central Asian countries in higher education
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Central Asian countries are set to strengthen cooperation in higher education, with a focus on student and academic mobility, as well as research and university partnerships. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir is in Astana, Kazakhstan, for a working visit until Sunday (Sept 27) to attend the Malaysia-Central Asia Ministerial Higher Education Meeting. The meeting is the first between Malaysia's Higher Education Minister and higher education ministers from Central Asian countries, opening the way for closer cooperation between higher-learning institutions in both regions.

items.title: Rupiah set for biggest weekly fall since May as higher US yields, stronger dollar bite
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Indonesia's rupiah was set for its biggest weekly fall since late May on Friday, pressured by rising US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and expectations that US interest rates will remain higher for longer. The rupiah extended losses, weakening as much as 0.3 per cent to 17,935 per dollar on the day. It has declined nearly one per cent so far this week.

items.title: Iran puts seven-day timeline on reopening Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: NEW YORK: Iran has submitted a proposal to the United States to end their war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, its foreign minister told media outlets in New York. "If certain conditions are met, the strait will be open within seven days and talks will start," Abbas Araghchi, who is in the US for the UN General Assembly, told media outlets including the New York Times and The Guardian. Araghchi also met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff.

items.title: PM’s brother Idrus Ibrahim buried in Bukit Mertajam after Friday prayers
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The remains of Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, were laid to rest at the Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Muslim Cemetery here today. The funeral was attended by hundreds of family members, relatives, friends and political leaders from various parties. The prime minister, accompanied by family members and members of the public, walked about 200 metres from the late Idrus’ home to the prayer hall.

items.title: Woman dies after Honda Jazz loses control, crashes into lorry in Kulai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 32-year-old woman with a hearing disability died after the Honda Jazz she was driving crashed into the rear of a lorry at KM32 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Air Hitam here early today. The woman, who worked as a general worker at a technology park in Kulai, suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, while the 66-year-old local lorry driver sustained minor injuries, Utusan Malaysia reported. Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the crash at about 6.15am.

items.title: Anwar thanks Cherok Tokun community for helping with brother's funeral
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim thanked members of the public and community leaders who attended and helped with the funeral arrangements for his late brother, Idrus Ibrahim. Thank you very much," Anwar told reporters after Idrus was laid to rest. Anwar had earlier taken time to personally greet and thank those who attended the funeral.

items.title: Foreigner fined RM3,000 for attempted wallet theft at Penang airport
items.summary: Magistrate Chia Huey Ting ordered Chen Bangjun, 55, to serve three months' jail if he fails to pay the fine. Section 379 provides for up to seven years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction, while Section 511 limits the jail term for an attempted offence to half of the maximum sentence. Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Sofi Jaafar urged the court to pass a deterrent sentence.

items.title: Vulnerable groups to be focus of Selangor Budget 2027, says MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Supporting vulnerable groups will be among the Selangor government’s main priorities in Budget 2027, with the aim of ensuring the state’s economic progress benefits people across all segments of society. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor’s development should go beyond strong economic performance and attracting investment to also addressing the needs of groups requiring greater attention, according to a Berita Harian report published today. Amirudin said existing support programmes, including cash handouts and assistance under Bantuan Kehidupan Sejahtera Selangor (Bingkas) and YANIS, would be part of efforts to help vulnerable groups, including those affected by the current energy supply crisis.

items.title: Selangor to explore more support for stressed doctors and nurses
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government will look into ways to ease the pressure on doctors and nurses serving in hospitals in the state. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said his administration was open to coordinating mental health and welfare assistance for healthcare workers facing stress. He said stress among healthcare workers may not be caused solely by workload.

items.title: Appeals court lets MAIWP strike out man’s bid to change religion from Islam to Sikhism
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Court of Appeal today allowed appeals by the Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) and the government to strike out a man’s suit challenging his religious status. The three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid ruled that Shehzad Malik Muhammad Sarwar Malik’s case was a renunciation case and the relief he is seeking could only be granted by the Syariah Court. “The respondent (Shehzad Malik) here cannot come to the Civil Court as the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to grant the orders,” said Justice Mohd Firuz, who delivered the unanimous decision.

items.title: 'Thank you, Cikgu': Steven Sim pays tribute to late headmaster, brother of PM Anwar
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim paid a moving tribute to his former primary school headmaster, the late Idrus Ibrahim. Idrus was the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Thank you, Cikgu," Sim said in his tribute.

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council established, first meeting in October
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has announced the establishment of the Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council to strengthen halal diplomacy between the two countries. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the council would be chaired by Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organizing Agency (BPJPH), while Malaysia would serve as its secretary-general. "Next month, the focus will be on facilitating halal certification between Malaysia and Indonesia to streamline bilateral halal trade between the two countries," he said in his speech at the Global Halal Summit 2026 here today.

items.title: Anwar wraps China visit with RM36.8b in trade, investment pledges
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, is not just a routine diplomatic trip, but rather a new benchmark for the continuation of strategic relations that strengthen cooperation in various fields between the two countries. The working visit at the invitation of the Chinese government not only strengthens bilateral relations, but also opens up new opportunities for Malaysia to expand investments, export markets and cooperation in strategic and high-value economic areas. Summarising the overall outcome of the visit, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the relationship between Malaysia and China is now at a very strong level and is developing positively.

items.title: Italy regulator closes P&G hair removal device probe after ad commitments
items.summary: ROME: Italy's antitrust authority (AGCM) said on Friday it had closed its investigation into US consumer goods maker Procter & Gamble's claims for a hair removal device, after the company committed to address the regulator's concerns. The AGCM opened an investigation in February into the allegedly misleading advertisements for the Braun Skin i-Expert pulsed light epilator, considering them exaggerated and not adequately demonstrated. P&G committed to remove the claim that the device could leave users free of body hair for two years, the watchdog said.

items.title: In Johor, Indonesian teen charged with trafficking over 25kg of illicit drugs
items.summary: The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The offense was also framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and is punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The charge was brought under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for illegal possession of drugs and is punishable under Section 39A(1) of the same Act.

items.title: 57,161 illegal immigrants detained in nationwide operations since January
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 57,161 undocumented migrants were detained in various enforcement operations nationwide between Jan 1 and Sept 13. The Immigration Department, in a statement, said 1,685 local employers were also detained for employing undocumented migrants during the period. "From Jan 1 to Sept 13, the department conducted 9,559 operations and inspected 128,536 individuals.

items.title: What is 'Taiwan independence' and what does that mean for Trump and Xi?
items.summary: WHAT IS TAIWAN'S HISTORY AND FORMAL NAME TODAY? Mao set up the People's Republic of China, and claimed it was the only legitimate Chinese government for the whole of China, including Taiwan, as the Republic of China's successor state. WHAT IS TAIWAN'S INTERNATIONAL STATUS AND CHINA'S POSITION?

items.title: Melaka election flood risk remains low, says meteorologist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The risk of major flooding during the Melaka election, expected in November, is low, but monsoon surges must be monitored, a meteorologist says. He said weather conditions during the election would also be influenced by the El Niño phenomenon, which could reduce the risk of prolonged rain that could cause major flooding. "November has already entered the Northeast Monsoon season.

items.title: KEB signs underwriting agreement ahead of ACE Market IPO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with M&A Securities Sdn Bhd ahead of its initial public offering (IPO) on the ACE Market. The IPO comprises a public issue of 138.54 million new shares and an offer for sale of 88.24 million existing shares, totalling 226.78 million shares. Another 22.06 million shares, or 2.5 per cent, will be placed with Bumiputera investors, while the remaining 50.3 million shares, or 5.7 per cent, are reserved for private placement to selected investors.

items.title: PNB targets RM15bil green investments under enhanced framework
items.summary: The country's largest fund manager is also targeting RM500 million in social investments under its enhanced Sustainability Framework 2026 (SF 2026). PNB said SF 2026 builds on its 2022 sustainability framework and aims to strengthen long-term resilience while ensuring that the value created from Malaysians' savings benefits future generations. Under SF 2026, PNB has identified three strategic anchors: story pension WISHadvancing organisational sustainability, responsible stewardship and strengthening the nation-building agenda.

items.title: Spell out the offence: Aminudin challenges Negeri MB over royal dispute allegations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on current Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to specify the alleged shortcomings of the previous administration that led to issues involving the state’s customary traditions and royal institution. Aminuddin said the public had the right to know what actions were allegedly not taken during his tenure as Menteri Besar, including the specific provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959 that were allegedly breached and when the alleged violation occurred. "What actions were said to have been overlooked?

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Undang, disputed chiefs: Conference of Rulers told of Tunku Nadzaruddin’s succession
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Negeri Sembilan government has notified the Conference of Rulers of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar’s selection as the state’s 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar, according to an Undang and three ruling chiefs whose positions are disputed. The group said the notification meant Tunku Nadzaruddin was the only person with lawful authority to perform the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959, including attending meetings of the Conference of Rulers, The Star reported today. “The state government administration must also immediately accord all privileges and entitlements prescribed for Tunku Nadzaruddin,” they said.

items.title: Anwar's brother laid to rest in Cherok Tokun
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's elder brother, Idrus Ibrahim, was laid to rest at the Cherok Tokun Bawah Muslim Cemetery after Friday prayers. The sombre gathering included Anwar, his children, close family members, villagers, community leaders and dignitaries who arrived to offer condolences to the bereaved family. Reflecting on the loss, Anwar expressed deep gratitude for his late brother's lifelong dedication, love and kindness towards the family.

items.title: [UPDATED] EC to hold special meeting on Oct 7 to set Melaka election date
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on Oct 7 to discuss arrangements for the 16th Melaka election following the dissolution of the state legislative assembly. In a statement today, EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the special meeting would be chaired by its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun. The meeting will determine key dates and other arrangements for the state election, including the issuance of the election writ, nomination day and polling day.

items.title: Google prepares to test AI chips in space
items.summary: SAN JOSE (California): Google will launch a prototype satellite to evaluate how its artificial intelligence (AI) chips perform in space, the company said on Thursday, reported German Press Agency (dpa). "In low Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth," Google said in a blog post. Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) will be loaded onto a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket next week to test how they handle the "physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space", Google said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan undangs tell PM, AGC to stay out of state affairs
items.summary: In a press conference in Seremban today, the group said Articles 10 and 11 of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 vested the Undang Yang Empat with exclusive authority to appoint and remove the state ruler, Free Malaysia Today reported. They also cautioned Anwar against using federal agencies in ways that could disrupt the administration of Negeri Sembilan. Do not sow disorder in our state using federal government agencies to paralyse the state government.

items.title: Melaka channels RM196m into schools, education aid for 140,000 children
items.summary: MELAKA: The Melaka government has allocated over RM196 million for school infrastructure development and educational assistance up to university level through the Melaka Sayang Rakyat (MeSRa) initiative, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. He said the allocation included a human capital empowerment programme benefiting over 140,000 children in Melaka. He said this when officiating the Sentuhan Kasih Ketua Menteri Melaka MeSRA Education Programme for the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) examinations, which was attended by state Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman.

items.title: 4 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four locations in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm, with Serian recording the highest reading at 174. The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Kuching recorded 162, followed by Samarahan at 161 and Sri Aman at 156. Three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah in Kelantan at 46, Langkawi in Kedah at 38 and Besut in Terengganu at 30.

items.title: Najib may walk out of Kajang Prison next month if High Court stays 15-year 1MDB sentence and RM50m fine is paid, says lawyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak could leave Kajang Prison as early as next month to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest if the High Court grants a stay of his 15-year 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) sentence, his lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said today. The High Court has fixed October 14 to hear Najib’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case pending his appeal. Shafee said the defence had sought the stay of the 1MDB sentence following the conditional pardon granted to Najib.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia form joint Halal Council to strengthen bilateral trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia announced the establishment of the Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council in a bid to strengthen halal diplomacy between the two countries, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today. "Next month, the focus is on facilitating halal certification between Malaysia and Indonesia to ease bilateral halal trade between the two countries," he said in his speech at the Global Halal Summit 2026 here today. Ahmad Zahid said the council would build on existing bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia to address differing halal requirements, repeated procedures and difficulties faced by businesses seeking to enter neighbouring markets.

items.title: Bandar Utama school stabbing: Family plans civil suit as mother asks if tragedy could have been prevented
items.summary: Her daughter, she said, is not coming home. she said. she said.

items.title: KTMB apologises after absent staff strands 25 riders at Anak Bukit station
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has apologised to affected passengers following an incident in which the Anak Bukit Station main gate failed to open as scheduled early this morning. KTMB said preliminary investigations found that the station was scheduled to begin operations at 5.30 am, but the staff member assigned to work failed to report for duty due to health reasons. “Immediate action was taken by instructing a counter clerk from a nearby station, who was scheduled to report for duty at 7 am, to arrive earlier at Anak Bukit Station,” KTMB said in a statement.

items.title: ‘Suspicion cannot take the place of proof’: BFM ordered to pay ex-presenter RM358,400 over 2019 dismissal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Industrial Court has ordered BFM Media Sdn Bhd to pay former producer and presenter Umapagan Ampikaipakan RM358,400 after ruling that the radio station failed to prove the misconduct allegations used to justify his dismissal in 2019. While the allegations against Umapagan were serious, Industrial Court chairman Pravin Kaur Jessy found that BFM had not proved the alleged misconduct on the balance of probabilities, The Edge Malaysia reported yesterday. BFM had accused Umapagan of sexual harassment and other misconduct, including sending explicit messages, making inappropriate remarks and engaging in unwanted physical contact.

items.title: Immigration busts Indonesians making RM50,000 monthly via illegal beauty treatments
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department (JIM) detained seven Indonesian nationals believed to be working as beauty therapists in a special operation at four locations in Shah Alam, Pandan Perdana and Kepong last Wednesday. JIM, in a statement today, said those detained comprised one man and six women aged between 19 and 44. JIM said two women and a man were detained under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while three women were detained under Section 6(1)(c) of the same Act.

items.title: Fadhlina: SMKA Jempol to become first TVET religious school in Malaysia
items.summary: JEMPOL, Sept 25 — Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama (SMKA) Jempol will become the country’s first Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) religious-stream school. Insya-Allah, SMKA Jempol will be the first SMKA to adopt or introduce TVET. Meanwhile, she said religious school students in the country were also encouraged to master various languages as an important medium for strengthening the dakwah agenda more effectively.

items.title: Chinese national fined RM3,000 over attempted wallet theft at Penang airport
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 55-year-old Chinese national was fined RM3,000 today after pleading guilty to attempting to steal a wallet from a man’s backpack at Penang International Airport last week, Harian Metro reported. Chen Bangjun entered the plea at the Magistrate’s Court in Balik Pulau after the charge was read to him in Mandarin before Magistrate Chia Huey Ting. According to the charge, Chen attempted to steal the wallet from a man’s backpack at the airport in Bayan Lepas between 9.25am and 10am on September 17.

items.title: KL public showers could make active lifestyles easier for working women, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Women working in Kuala Lumpur could be among the biggest beneficiaries of better public shower facilities, as the city moves to improve basic amenities through an architectural design competition. Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said public showers could provide women with a more comfortable place to freshen up before work, particularly as Kuala Lumpur makes greater use of its green and recreational spaces. This public shower facility is very important for women.

items.title: Anwar returns to Cheruk Tok Kun for final farewell to late brother Idrus
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today paid his last respects to his elder brother, Idrus, who passed away yesterday evening. Anwar arrived at his family home in Cheruk Tok Kun here at 11.05 am with his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. Also present were Penang Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid; Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim; Penang Mufti Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Sukki Othman; Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Kheng; and political leaders from various parties.

items.title: PAS unfazed by Perikatan suspension, says voters already know its moon symbol
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — PAS is prepared to contest future elections under its own moon symbol if Perikatan Nasional (PN) is unable to use its coalition logo, party vice-president Datuk Mohd Amar Nik Abdullah said. Mohd Amar said PAS was sufficiently well known among voters for a change of electoral symbol not to pose a problem, pointing to recognition of the party in recent state elections. Mohd Amar said that if PAS was unable to use the PN logo, reverting to its traditional moon symbol would not pose a problem.

items.title: MCMC steps in to address WhatsApp account fraud in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is looking into public complaints regarding WhatsApp accounts that have reportedly been compromised, blocked, or rendered inaccessible. “Affected users are advised to use official WhatsApp channels for account recovery or verification,” the statement read. According to MCMC, account compromised and account blocking are two distinct issues.

items.title: Two Perak tahfiz students, 13 and 14, charged over alleged iron attack on classmate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Two boys aged 13 and 14 have been charged with injuring a 13-year-old fellow student by allegedly pressing an iron against his chest at a tahfiz school in Perak Tengah. According to Utusan Malaysia , both students pleaded not guilty when the charge was read to them before Magistrate Nurul Izalina Rajaai at the Magistrate’s Court in Parit today. According to the victim’s account, two fellow students had allegedly pressed an iron against his chest, causing the injuries.

items.title: Najib’s bank accounts frozen, cannot afford RM50m fine, says lawyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak cannot afford the RM50 million fine imposed as a condition for him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest, his lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said today. “As of today, Datuk Seri Najib himself cannot afford to pay it. He also said Najib had never sought public donations to help settle the RM50 million fine.

items.title: Tributes pour in for PM’s late brother Idrus Ibrahim from Cabinet members
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Several Cabinet ministers have expressed their condolences to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his family following the passing of his elder brother, Idrus Ibrahim, yesterday. In a Facebook post, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu described the loss of a brother as deeply painful. Meanwhile, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said he was also deeply saddened by the news of Idrus’ passing and understood the grief Anwar was experiencing following the loss of a loved one.

items.title: Ex-Tabung Haji COO Adi Azuan hit with further charge over home renovations
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Public Prosecutor Irna Julieza Maaras informed the court that the accused had been charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court yesterday under a similar section, and the prosecution requested that the RM50,000 bail and bail conditions imposed by that court be applied to this case. The Shah Alam Sessions Court also set Nov 25 for mention of the case. Therefore, we ask the court to apply the bail and bail conditions imposed by that court to this case,” he said.

items.title: Cash ‘vanishes’ mid-air: Cops hunt foreign national after RM60,000 goes missing from passenger’s backpack on KL-Penang flight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A passenger arrived in Penang yesterday only to discover that RM60,000 in cash had allegedly gone missing from his backpack during a flight from Kuala Lumpur. The 54-year-old victim reported the suspected theft after landing at Penang International Airport, with police now seeking a foreign national believed to have been on the same flight, the New Straits Times reported. South-west district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said the victim suspected the foreign passenger was involved in the incident.

items.title: Driver flees crash scene in Kedah, leaves behind RM6m cannabis haul in MPV
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A man’s escape from the scene after the MPV he was driving was involved in a crash on the southbound North-South Expressway near Kota Setar, Kedah, led police to uncover 72kg of cannabis flowers worth nearly RM6 million in the vehicle. Police from Kedah then inspected the Toyota Wish and found four luggage bags inside. A source said each bag contained 30 plastic packets believed to contain cannabis.

items.title: Rais Yatim pleads not guilty to sedition charge over Negeri Sembilan royal crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Dr Rais Yatim today pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court to a sedition charge linked to the Negeri Sembilan royal crisis in June. The 84-year-old entered the plea after the charge was read out by a court interpreter before Judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin, Astro Awani reported.
